power/sq: Derivatives follow rules, so the limit is rarely needed. For x squared, bring the two down in front and lower the power by one: two x.
power/cube: x cubed becomes three x squared.
power/rule: In general, x to the n becomes n times x to the n minus one. That is the power rule.
power/check: Check it at x equals two. The measured slope of x cubed is twelve, and three times two squared is twelve.
sums/factor: A number in front comes along for the ride. Five x cubed becomes five times three x squared: fifteen x squared.
sums/sum: A sum is differentiated one term at a time. Two x is a line with slope two.
sums/zero: A constant on its own is flat, so its derivative is zero. The seven drops out.
sums/whole: So five x cubed plus two x plus seven has derivative fifteen x squared plus two.
explog/ex: e to the x is special: it is its own derivative. At every point, its slope equals its height.
explog/eax: With a number multiplying x in the power, that number comes out in front: e to the three x has derivative three e to the three x.
explog/ln: And ln x has derivative one over x: steep near zero, flatter as x grows. At x equals two, its slope is a half.
example/ask: Your turn to follow along. What is the derivative of four x cubed minus three x squared plus five?
example/t1: Term by term. In four x cubed, the three comes down: four times three is twelve, so twelve x squared.
example/t2: Minus three x squared becomes minus six x.
example/t3: The five is a constant, so it drops out. The derivative is twelve x squared minus six x.
